The Arq8™ Dosing Guide

How to Use Creatine for Your Specific Goal

Start Here: Creatine Works Through Saturation.

Creatine doesn't work like caffeine. There's no acute hit, no spike, no same-day effect. It works by saturating your muscle and brain tissue with stored cellular energy — phosphocreatine, the fastest-acting energy currency your body produces. Once those reserves are full, every contraction, every cognitive demand, every recovery process runs on a deeper battery.

Getting to saturation takes 2–4 weeks of daily intake. Staying there is what unlocks the full benefit profile.

The dose that gets you there depends on what you're optimizing for. Most people only need to know one tier. Some will benefit from two. A few specific scenarios call for the third.

The Three Tiers

○ Foundation

5g | 4 gummies

Default for everyone. Muscle, baseline brain, longevity.

Optimization

10g | 4 gummies + 1 scoop powder

Brain saturation, cognitive performers, women's health, high training load.

○ Acute Rescue

20–25g | 4–5 scoops powder

Sleep deprivation events, jet lag, deadline weeks.

TIER 1
FOUNDATION 5 g/day
FOUNDATION | 5 g/day

Who this is for: Almost everyone starting with creatine. Recreational athletes, active professionals, anyone building daily consistency for the first time.

The dose: 4 gummies daily. Same time, every day.

What it covers:

1 Full muscle creatine saturation within 3–4 weeks
2 Strength, training output, recovery
3 Baseline brain creatine support
4 Long-term muscle preservation, bone density, metabolic health
5 Cardiovascular and hormonal foundations

Timing: Flexible. Morning with coffee, post-workout, with dinner — what matters is daily consistency, not the clock. If you train, post-workout pairs slightly better with insulin-driven uptake, but the difference is marginal compared to the impact of taking it every day.

What to expect: Subtle in week one. Noticeable by week three. Categorically different by month three.

TIER 2
OPTIMIZATION 10 g/day
OPTIMIZATION | 10 g/day

Who this is for: People optimizing for cognitive performance, women prioritizing brain, mood, and hormonal support, and individuals under sustained training or mental load.

Why the higher dose: The brain is harder to saturate than muscle. Creatine crosses the blood-brain barrier slowly. Muscle reaches full saturation at 5 g/day. Brain creatine elevation — the kind that supports cognitive resilience, mood stability, and sleep-deprivation tolerance — typically requires around 10 g/day for 4–8 weeks before plateauing.


This is the dose where the research on creatine's cognitive, mood, and women's health applications lives. Most brands don't talk about it because most brands position creatine as a gym supplement. The evidence supports going further.

The dose: 4 gummies + 1 scoop (5 g) of Arq8™ FullDissolve™ Powder daily.

Why stack Gummies + Powder: At 10 g/day, doubling the gummy serving (8 gummies) becomes impractical — calorie and cost load both increase. The Powder is the efficient way to deliver the second 5 g. FullDissolve™ dissolves clear into coffee, water, or any liquid you're already drinking. No second routine to remember.

Specific applications at this tier:

1 Cognitive performers: professionals under high mental load, executives, knowledge workers, students
2 Women optimizing for brain, mood, and hormonal balance: women have lower baseline muscle creatine stores than men and research increasingly supports higher daily intake for female-specific applications
3 High training volume: endurance athletes, CrossFit, double-session days
4 Sleep-disrupted lifestyles: parents, shift workers, frequent travelers

Timing: Split if preferred — gummies in the morning, powder with afternoon coffee or post-training. Single dose is fine too.

TIER 3
ACUTE RESCUE 20–25 g, occasional
ACUTE RESCUE | 20–25 g, occasional

Who this is for: Anyone facing a known cognitive performance event under sleep deprivation. Not a daily protocol — a strategic tool.

The research: A 2024 study (Gordji-Nejad et al.) found that a single dose of 0.35 g/kg body weight — roughly 20–25 g for most adults — produced measurable cognitive and metabolic benefits within 3–4 hours during 21 hours of sleep deprivation. This was a one-time acute dose, not a daily protocol.

The dose: 4–5 scoops (20–25 g) of Arq8™ FullDissolve™ Powder, taken 3–4 hours before the cognitive demand window.

Why Powder, not Gummies: 20 g of creatine in gummy form would mean 16+ gummies — impractical in calorie load, cost, and texture. The Powder is the only sensible format at this dose, and FullDissolve™ is the only form that dissolves cleanly at this volume without GI discomfort.

When to use it:

1 Major deadline or exam after a poor night's sleep
2 Long-haul flight crossing multiple time zones
3 New parent surviving a hard night
4 Performance events where mental clarity matters and sleep wasn't on your side

Important context: This is not a substitute for sleep, and it's not designed for daily use at this dose. Daily intake at 20+ g exceeds the safety profile the clinical literature supports and is unnecessary for any chronic application.

HOW TO CHOOSE YOUR TIER

Start at Tier 1

if you're new to creatine or returning after a break. Run it for at least 4 weeks. Most people don't need to go further.

Move to Tier 2 if any of these apply:
  • Cognitive performance is your primary outcome
  • You're a woman optimizing for mood, hormonal balance, or brain health
  • Your training volume is high and recovery is the bottleneck
  • You've been on Tier 1 for 6+ weeks and want to push the brain-specific benefits the research supports
Use Tier 3

as a tool, not a routine. Build it into specific high-demand events when you need it.

WHAT DOESN'T CHANGE

A few things are worth being clear about, because the supplement industry is full of noise on these:

1 Loading is optional.

You can take 4 gummies twice a day for 5–7 days to reach saturation faster, or just take 4 gummies daily and reach saturation in 3–4 weeks. Both work.

2 Cycling is not required.

Creatine is taken continuously. There's no benefit to stopping and restarting.

3 Timing is flexible.

Take it when it fits your routine. Daily consistency outperforms perfect timing.

4 Gender doesn't lower the dose.

Women need at least 5 g/day. For brain, mood, and hormonal applications, the research increasingly supports going higher — not lower.

5 Hydration matters.

Drink water normally. Creatine doesn't require excessive water intake — that's a myth from the 1990s.

TAURINE

Cellular stability for calm energy and endurance. Taurine is highly concentrated in the heart, brain, and muscles. It regulates cellular hydration, electrolyte balance, and calcium signaling — essential for sustained performance. Unlike stimulants, it supports energy by stabilizing the nervous system and protecting cells from oxidative stress.

ZINC (AS ZINC PICOLINATE)

Essential for recovery, immunity, and hormonal health. Zinc is required for over 300 enzymatic reactions, including DNA repair, immune defense, and protein synthesis. Zinc picolinate is a highly bioavailable form that supports tissue repair, hormonal balance, and antioxidant protection — all foundational for recovery and long-term health.
  • Supports immune function*
  • Aids tissue repair and recovery*
  • Supports healthy testosterone levels*
  • Contributes to antioxidant defense*
  • Supports skin health and wound healing*

SUCCINIC ACID (SUCCINATE)

Mitochondrial fuel for sustained cellular energy. Succinic acid is a key intermediate in the Krebs cycle — the energy-producing pathway inside mitochondria. Supplementing supports ATP generation, improving endurance, oxygen utilization, and metabolic efficiency during prolonged physical or mental demand.
  • Supports ATP production in mitochondria*
  • Enhances endurance and stamina*
  • Aids oxygen utilization during exercise*
  • Reduces fatigue under physical demand*

Myth: creatine is only for men

Women naturally produce 20–40% less creatine than men — and levels fluctuate further during menstrual cycles, perimenopause, and menopause. Creatine supports lean muscle, cognitive clarity, mood stability, and bone density. Women don't just benefit from creatine — they may need it more.

Myth: creatine is only for the gym

Your brain consumes creatine too. It supports mental energy, focus under stress, and resilience on low-sleep days.

Myth: creatine = bulky look

Creatine doesn't make you bulky. It supports strength, tone, and recovery by helping your muscles recycle energy faster. How you look depends on how you train and eat. Creatine just makes your effort go further.

Myth: creatine makes you bloated

Old-generation creatine doesn't dissolve fully — large particles sit outside the cell, pull water, and cause that puffy, bloated feeling. FullDissolve™ Nano-Creatine is engineered for complete solubility. It absorbs efficiently, gets into the cell, and doesn't cause water retention, bloating or GI discomfort.

Myth: creatine damages your kidneys

It has been clinically proven that creatine does not damage kidneys. In healthy individuals, 5g daily of creatine monohydrate shows no adverse effects on kidney function — even in long-term use. This myth comes from confusing creatine with creatinine, a waste marker. They're not the same thing.

Myth: creatine gummies are just candy

Most are. Many contain less creatine than claimed, use cheap forms that don't absorb well, and coat with sugar. Every batch of Arq8 is third-party tested and provides a verified 5g clinical dose of FullDissolve™ Nano-Creatine — plus Taurine, Succinic Acid, and Zinc. This isn't candy. It's a scientifically formulated functional gummy.

Questions?
We've got answers.

Is creatine safe for daily use?

Yes. Creatine is one of the most studied supplements in existence — with over 700 clinical studies and 30+ years of research confirming its safety for long-term daily use in healthy adults. No cycling required.

When should I take creatine?

Any time. Creatine doesn't work like a stimulant — it works by maintaining consistent levels in your muscle and brain tissue around the clock. Morning, evening, with food or without. The only thing that matters is taking it every day.

Will this cause bloating?

Not with Arq8™. Bloating from creatine is caused by undissolved particles sitting in the gut. FullDissolve™ Nano-Creatine dissolves completely — which means nothing sits unabsorbed, and your digestive system never has to deal with the residue that causes discomfort.

Is creatine only for athletes?

No. Your brain uses creatine just as much as your muscles do. Creatine supports mental clarity, focus, stress resilience, and cognitive performance under fatigue — making it as relevant for professionals, parents, and anyone under daily demand as it is for athletes.

When will I start seeing results?

Most people notice subtle improvements in energy and focus within the first one to two weeks. Full muscle and brain saturation typically occurs around 30 days of consistent daily use — which is when the deeper benefits become most noticeable.

Does creatine have any side effects?

Creatine is exceptionally well tolerated. The side effects most people associate with it — bloating, cramping, digestive discomfort — are caused by poor solubility in standard forms, not by creatine itself. FullDissolve™ eliminates those issues. No stimulants. No hormones. Nothing artificial.
